It's like a text-based interface as supposed to the browser interface. A REST API is basically four function parts.

  1. The URL that defines what action to take with arguments separated by / char. For example, https://domain.com/my-api/delete-this/with-id-x tells the server to delete something which has id x. The URLs are usually designed to be self-explanatory to their functions.
  2. The header, in this case we can ignore it once been setup.
  3. The body part which contains more specific parameters, usually in JSON document format(it's just a key-value based text format). For example, { "username" : "Germ22", "password" : "Hey I am your new Hitler", "TokenID" : "some id issued from the server" } will identify yourself with your username/password etc with its associated values. The "username" is the key, and the "Germ22" is the value. The values can be nested with other key-value structure.
  4. The response returned from the server, usually in the same document format as #3. The return responses are also usually self-explanatory, close enough to reading a short English sentence or two. The descriptive nature will usually tell us exactly what the outcome is from the execution. This is the part where we observe conditions like "Exception: something went wrong", or "Server error", or possibly spits out the 404, 500 status like you have reported it before during the preview test. :-) You should be able to identify just by reading the responses.

:-) I believe you can be very helpful. But it takes some effort and patience to setup this standalone app and read the document that tells you which URL with what arguments(body part) to send. Once you get a hang of it, it is not much different from the browser interface. Instead of filling out the textbox on a form or clicking the submit buttons, you are now sending a formatted text to the server and reading the response text back from the server.
